result.summary: lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex is a genuinely pure module: grep for Repo./Logger./Process./GenServer./spawn/:ets./raise/rescue/try across both changed files returns zero hits (only doc-comment mentions), matching the moduledoc's own stated purity claim and Letflow.Engine.Transition's existing precedent -- no fake-purity crutch (evaluate_condition/2's with/else composition folds every error stage into `false` structurally, never via rescue). Supervision integrity is N/A as expected: no process/GenServer/InstanceSupervisor involvement in either file, confirmed by inspection rather than assumed. transition_error()'s new {:no_matching_edge, node_id, evaluated_conditions} variant follows the file's existing tagged-tuple-with-named-fields convention (matches :unknown_node_id, :gateway_not_yet_implemented shape); evaluated_condition() is a 3-key map (edge_id, condition, result) consistent with Graph.Edge.t()'s condition/is_default fields and is used identically at its one call site (evaluate_conditioned_edges/3) and one construction site (dispatch_exclusive_gateway/4's error branch) -- no drift. Scope stayed within REQ-050's boundary: dispatch_parallel_gateway/4 and its stub comment are untouched (diff shows only a preceding hunk's context line shifting), no REQ-061 error-handling machinery (retry, ERROR-state transition, persistence) was built -- the {:no_matching_edge, ...} tuple is returned to the caller, not itself transitioned into any instance ERROR state, matching design doc's own scope note. docs/anti-patterns.md has no entries this diff re-triggers (checked fragment/1 duplication, docker-worktree, timestamp entries -- none apply to a pure evaluator addition). docs/migration/decisions/ -- none contradicted: 0001/0002/0003 (web framework, OIDC, Ecto schema strategy) are untouched surface area, 0006 (schema-per-tenant identity tables) is irrelevant to a DB-free pure module. On the two failing tests (transition_test.exs:334, variable_merge_test.exs:302): this is the correct, expected consequence of REQ-050 legitimately superseding the REQ-044 :EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY stub, not a regression. Both assertions pin the literal {:error, {:gateway_not_yet_implemented, :EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY, ...}} stub tuple that dispatch_exclusive_gateway/4 no longer returns by design -- the requirement's whole point was replacing that stub with real dispatch. The sibling :PARALLEL_GATEWAY stub assertion (transition_test.exs:353) is untouched and still correct, confirming the failures are localized to exactly the code path this requirement changed, not a wider breakage. Updating those two assertions to the new real-dispatch behavior is correctly TEST-DESIGNER's Step 3 work, not a REVIEWER blocker.
